category_law: Synthetic carriers only. Not survey-semantic equivalence. Zero real survey sources opened.

independent_exercises.why_separate: These are deliberately NOT the candidate's own courts. Each commissioned property was exercised directly against the candidate, so a court that had drifted or softened would still be caught.

exercises.evidence: cap = 703 (exactly the bytes the reader needs) -> refused = False, consumed = 703. An exactly-enough ceiling completes and is NOT treated as a breach.
cap = 702 -> refused with READER_BYTES_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, consumed exactly 702. The refusal is precise at the boundary.

Eight-ceiling sweep: caps 1, 7, 64, 199, 702, 703, 704, 2109 against a 703-byte requirement. Consumed <= cap in every case; breach = none. At caps 704 and 2109 consumption stops at 703 because that is all the reader wanted.

exercises.property: no callback exception as the limiting mechanism
exercises.evidence: The governed view was driven directly under an armed allowance of 24. No exception propagated out of read() (raised_inside_read = False). The served chunk sequence was [24, 0] -- exactly the allowance, then a clean b'' end-of-stream -- with truncated_or_exhausted recorded on the governed open. The limit is therefore enforced by SHORTENING and EOF, never by an exception crossing the bridge.

Naive reuse of ONE view object across two row_offset parses FAILED (ReadstatError), confirming the constraint is real. Issuing a fresh position-zero view per parse over the SAME physical open then produced correct disjoint chunks: chunk0 = [0.0, 1.0], chunk1 = [2.0, 3.0] on a 60-row DTA. physical_opens = 1 with 3 views issued.

exercises.property: chunk_rows honoured on a carrier larger than one chunk
exercises.evidence: A 200-row, 3-column SAV iterated at batch_size 30. rows_per_chunk = 30 // 3 = 10, so 20 chunk reads were required and 20 were issued. All 200 row ordinals were covered, no batch exceeded 30 cells, path_opens stayed at 1, and every V00 value matched float(i) exactly in order.

selected route on a 3-column SAV selecting V01: selected_reads = 1, full_reads = 0, metadata_reads = 1, reader_bytes = 2846, bound_ordinals = [2]. Each quantity is its own account and none proxies for another.

exercises.property: selected route does not silently claim byte suppression
exercises.evidence: Selected-route reader_bytes = 2846 versus full-route reader_bytes = 703 on the same carrier -- the selected route moves MORE physical bytes, not fewer, because usecols subsets after a full stream read. This corroborates the disclosure rather than contradicting it, and shows no physical suppression is being claimed anywhere.

self_correction_recorded.what_happened: The first run of the independent exercises reported 8/9 with the DTA exercise marked FAIL.
self_correction_recorded.diagnosis: The candidate was correct and MY EXPECTATION was wrong. The exercise builds V00 as float(i) * (c + 1) with c == 0, so V00 holds 0,1,2,3...; I had asserted chunk0 == [0.0, 2.0] and chunk1 == [4.0, 6.0], wrongly applying a factor of 2.
self_correction_recorded.observed_actual: chunk0 = [0.0, 1.0], chunk1 = [2.0, 3.0] -- which is exactly correct.
self_correction_recorded.action: The expectation was corrected to float(i) semantics and the exercise re-run. The candidate was NOT modified.
self_correction_recorded.why_recorded: A FAIL line that is really a bad assertion is exactly the kind of thing that gets quietly suppressed. It is disclosed instead, and the correction is to the test, not to the code.
